name: Myers Compactified Black Hole
description: An extremal electrically charged black hole localized on a compact spatial circle in five dimensional Einstein-Maxwell theory, with a round 3-sphere horizon and an infinite throat.
history: Follow a circle through space and you return to where you started. Put a charged black hole in a universe with such a direction and its gravity reaches around the circle [horowitzmaeda2002]. Robert C. Myers constructed black holes with compact spatial dimensions in 1987, extending the solutions of Sudhansu Datta Majumdar and Achilles Papapetrou to higher dimensions [horowitzmaeda2002, myers1987compact]. The holes carry enough electric charge for their repulsion to balance their gravitational attraction [horowitzmaeda2002].¶The five dimensional solution has one time and four spatial dimensions, with one spatial direction curled into a circle. Its line element is $ds^2=-U^{-2}dt^2+U(dr^2+r^2d\Omega_2^2+dz^2)$, with $c=1$ and $d\Omega_2^2=d\theta^2+\sin^2\theta\,d\phi^2$ [horowitzmaeda2002, myers1987compact]. Here $r$ is the radial coordinate in the three extended spatial directions, $z$ has period $L$, and $\mu>0$ sets the charge and mass of the hole [horowitzmaeda2002]. The harmonic function is $U=1+\frac{\pi\mu}{Lr}\frac{\sinh(2\pi r/L)}{\cosh(2\pi r/L)-\cos(2\pi z/L)}$ [horowitzmaeda2002, myers1987compact]. Spherical coordinates centred on the hole have $r=\rho\sin\chi$ and $z=\rho\cos\chi$ [gilmore2009caged].¶Unroll the circle and the single hole becomes an infinite row of identical holes separated by $L$ [horowitzmaeda2002]. The electric potential is proportional to $U^{-1}$ [suzuki2012caged]. The periodicity of $U$ identifies each hole with its neighbors and leaves one horizon in the compact space [horowitzmaeda2002]. Far from the hole the circle has circumference $L$, and the dependence on $z$ falls off exponentially [horowitzmaeda2002].¶The horizon lies at $r=z=0$, where $U$ diverges [horowitzmaeda2002]. Near it the geometry approaches that of a single extremal black hole in five dimensions, and its horizon is a round 3-sphere with area $2\pi^2\mu^{3/2}$ [horowitzmaeda2002]. The proper distance down a static slice to the horizon is infinite [horowitzmaeda2002]. The circle grows toward the hole, making room for a horizon of any size even when $L$ is small [horowitzmaeda2002].¶A separate family of uncharged black holes also lives in a space with a compact direction [kol2006caged]. As a hole in that family grows, its horizon stretches along the circle [kol2006caged]. In six dimensions the black hole branch, followed numerically, merges with a nonuniform black string branch [kol2006caged]. The string's horizon wraps the circle, while the horizon of the charged hole remains a 3-sphere [kol2006caged, horowitzmaeda2002].

related.text: The extremal charged holes in four dimensions, held at rest by the same balance of electric repulsion and gravity [horowitzmaeda2002, majumdar1947, papapetrou1947].
A horizon that wraps the compact direction; the uncharged black hole and nonuniform string branches meet in a separate family of vacuum solutions [kol2006caged].
A spherical black hole in higher dimensions with no charge; its five dimensional horizon is a 3-sphere [kol2006caged, tangherlini1963].
Rotating vacuum black holes in higher dimensions, with a spherical horizon in five dimensions [kol2006caged, myers1986].
Extremal charged black holes in a universe with a positive cosmological constant, moving with its expansion or contraction [kastor1993].
A five dimensional vacuum geometry with a compact circle that closes at its centre; the monopole has no horizon [horowitz2012, grossperry1983].
Charged black holes seen from four dimensions in a five dimensional vacuum geometry with a compact circle [horowitz2012].
